conventions.convention: SI units are used. The positive action reference h_* is a normalization convention, not identified with Planck's constant. Ordered identical-particle phase space carries dν_N=dq dp/(N! h_*^(3N)).

Reference-relative entropy requires absolute integrability of ρ log ρ, with 0 log 0=0. Gibbs-volume entropy is k_B log Ω; surface entropy is k_B log(Ω' ΔE) with fixed positive energy width. Temperature is the reciprocal entropy derivative and capacity the reciprocal temperature derivative where defined.
The softened model has fixed a>0 on a bounded Lebesgue measurable positive-volume region. The point-particle Hamiltonian is a distinct model, not the definition evaluated at a=0.

The relative Kepler model has r_0≤|q|≤R, R>16r_0, and measure dq dp/h_*^3 with neither center-of-mass variables nor an identical-particle factorial. Its selected negative-energy branch is A/R<e≤A/(16r_0), E=−e.
At e=A/(16r_0), entropy and temperature derivatives are right derivatives in E from within the selected branch; capacity is the reciprocal of that one-sided temperature derivative.
Canonical response varies β while the Hamiltonian, regulator, box, particle count and reference measure remain fixed; T_K=1/(k_B β).

The static gas uses a prescribed smooth background with uniformly positive bounded lapse, uniformly positive-definite spatial metric, x^0=ct, local orthonormal momentum, and dV_h d³p̂=d³x d³p_i. No gas backreaction is assumed.
Finite-bath dynamical stability concerns only the separately adopted scalar law dx/dt=L S_tot'(x), L>0, near an interior critical point with strictly negative second derivative.

The supplied finite Fermi occupation result explicitly assumes Countable Choice and the current draft occupation-trace interface; authoring readiness and precheck are not independent supplier approval.

load_bearing.statement: For the finite softened model and every β>0, the displayed Gaussian lower and upper bounds give 0<Z_N(β)<∞. Every absolute energy moment is finite; Z_N is C∞ with Z_N^(j)(β)=∫(−H_(N,a))^j exp(−βH_(N,a)) dν_N. On compact positive β intervals an integrable majorant works for each fixed derivative order.

On the specified relative shell and branch, Ω(−e)=[(4π)(4π/3)(2μ)^(3/2)A³/h_*³] e^(−3/2) J(er_0/A). The shell measure is the specified pushforward with density μ p_*/h_*³, normalized by Ω'(E); the selected entropy is Gibbs volume.

The two-equal-mass point model in a bounded box with interior has infinite canonical partition integral for every β>0. The specified fixed-softening growing-box sequence and fixed-density hard-core sequence have log Z_N/N→+∞, hence free energy per particle and per volume tending to −∞.
On the specified regulated branch, T_G=e/(k_B B(δ)) and C_G=−k_B B(δ)²/[B(δ)−δB'(δ)]<0, with denominator at least 1 and the stated one-sided endpoint convention.

For the prescribed bounded-lapse static background, 0<Z_1<∞, polynomial momentum moments and compact-positive-β_K derivatives are finite, Z_M=Z_1^M/M!, and Ξ=exp(zZ_1). The defined local densities satisfy T_loc=T_K/N, P=n k_B T_loc, and ∂_iP=−(ε+P)∂_i log N.

For probability densities with absolutely integrable ρ log ρ and energy, S(ρ)−k_B β〈H〉_ρ≤k_B log Z_N, with equality exactly at p_β almost everywhere. At equal mean energy p_β is the unique entropy maximizer; the stated bounded centered perturbations have the displayed quadratic relative-entropy expansion and cubic remainder bound.

At common positive temperature and finite nonzero capacities, S_tot''=−T^(−2)(1/C_1+1/C_2). For C_1<0<C_2, C_2<|C_1| gives a strict local entropy maximum. Under the separately specified exchange equation, a nondegenerate local maximum attracts a compact neighborhood exponentially for all forward times.

concerns.concern: The Statement says: “on every compact positive β interval one integrable majorant justifies all derivatives of Z_rel.” Step 1.2 instead supplies a majorant B_j(1+|p|^(2j)) exp(−β_0|p|²/(2μ)) for each fixed order j. A single finite majorant simultaneously dominating the unscaled derivative integrands for every j cannot exist: at a fixed β, |h|^j exp(−βh) grows without bound as j→∞ wherever the numerical energy magnitude exceeds 1, a set of positive phase measure. The statement needs the fixed-order qualification already present in lem-tgr-finite-gravitational-gibbs. The normalization and response formulas themselves are supported by the order-dependent envelopes.
